A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same algorithms and case studies. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original evaluations of ski-rental algorithms using CitiBike data and scheduling predictors using sepsis clinical records.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report empirical algorithm comparisons, predictor evaluations, and feature and parameter analyses for CitiBike and sepsis scheduling.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 3 retain the same inputs, thresholds, and decision rules. V3 discusses choosing a larger existing calibration-error bound. Its altered interpolation description in Section 3.2 conflicts with the unchanged Algorithm 1 rather than establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use June 2015 CitiBike rides and Sepsis Survival Minimal Clinical Records for the same tasks. Appendix C retains the same destination-information scenarios and patient population; no dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: The corresponding ski-rental comparisons retain Breakeven, Anand et al.'s Binary method, and Sun et al.'s Conformal method. Scheduling retains the comparison against Cho et al.'s binary-based calibration across the same predictor families.

E3.justification: The reported predictor configurations, preprocessing, break-even sweeps, and scheduling evaluations with n = 100 and varying costs and θ are retained. Section 2 renames the additive cost difference as regret without changing its formula or the evaluated metric.

E4.justification: Both retain Appendix C's feature-information comparisons, alternative predictor analyses, and parameter sweeps. No empirical ablation or robustness test is added or removed; the new robustness discussion in Section 3.3 is theoretical.

E5.justification: The same shaded bands and Figure 5 error bars appear in both versions. Neither adds run counts, seeds, confidence levels, explanations of uncertainty estimation, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The empirical plots in Figures 2–9 retain identical results, including all Appendix C panels. Numerical findings in the accompanying text, such as the sepsis predictor's AUC of 0.86, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B generalizes the scheduling derivation from perfect calibration to monotonic calibration, introducing Z = Pr[Y = 1 | f(X)] and variance terms based on Z. Section 3.3 adds an explicit piecewise worst-case robustness bound g(α) and its justification. These additions substantially broaden the theoretical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract changes ski-rental performance from 'optimal' to 'near-optimal,' although Section 1.1 retains optimality for calibrated predictors. The conclusion explicitly qualifies applicability to distributional performance and useful binary-target probability estimates. The two central case-study contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 explains how increasing the calibration-error bound trades expected performance for worst-case robustness and discusses scheduling applicability without perfect calibration. The conclusion adds specific open directions involving binary cross-entropy and expected calibration error, refining the work's practical boundaries.

D1.justification: V3 adds a Section 5 footnote identifying a repository for code and data; v1 mentions implementation without providing that access information. Existing dataset links, features, model descriptions, and calibration details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds distributional-prediction research and distinguishes it from uncertainty quantification. V3 also adds scheduling-regret and probabilistic-forecasting references and changes the probabilistic-guarantees citation to Gupta et al. (2022). The central positioning against conformal predictions and binary scheduling advice remains.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites refine the introduction's trust framing, distinguish competitive ratio from additive regret, adopt 'learning-augmented' terminology, and expand the conclusion. Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections are added, while the main section sequence and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, with extensive resizing and redistribution of figures, tables, and equations. Caption and header styles change. V1's Table 3, a duplicate of Table 1, is removed; Figures 1–9 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V3 improves theoretical usefulness through the explicit robustness discussion and scheduling proof under weaker calibration assumptions, while adding clearer applicability boundaries and code/data access information. These are meaningful gains over v1. Their benefit is tempered by remaining inconsistencies, including the revised Section 3.2 rental-time description conflicting with Algorithm 1, so the overall improvement is limited.
